items.stem: A sum of Rs. 280 is to be used towards four prizes. If each prize after the first is Rs. 20 less than its preceding prize, find the value of each of the prizes.
items.answer:
Let the first prize be Rs. x. Then the prizes form the AP x, x − 20, x − 40, x − 60, so a = x, d = −20 and n = 4, with S₄ = 280.
Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] gives 280 = 4/2[2x + 3(−20)] = 2[2x − 60], so 140 = 2x − 60 and x = 200/2 = 100.
Hence the four prizes are Rs. 100, Rs. 80, Rs. 60 and Rs. 40.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem: In a garden bed, there are 23 rose plants in the first row, 21 are in the 2ⁿᵈ, 19 in the 3ʳᵈ row and so on. There are 5 plants in the last row. How many rows are there of rose plants? Also find the total number of rose plants in the garden.
items.answer:
The plants per row are 23, 21, 19, …, 5, an AP with a = 23 and d = −2, and the last term aₙ = 5.
aₙ = a + (n − 1)d gives 5 = 23 + (n − 1)(−2), so (n − 1)(−2) = −18 and n = 10. There are 10 rows.
Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] gives S₁₀ = 10/2[2(23) + 9(−2)] = 5(46 − 18) = 5 × 28 = 140.
So there are 10 rows and 140 rose plants in all.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem: A sum of Rs. 1890 is to be used to given seven cash prizes to students of a school for their overall academic performance. If each prize is Rs. 50 less than its preceding prize, find the value of each of the prizes.
items.answer:
Let the first prize be Rs. x. The prizes form the AP x, x − 50, x − 100, x − 150, …, so a = x, d = −50, n = 7 and S₇ = 1890.
Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] gives 1890 = 7/2[2x + (−50) × 6], so 540 = 2x − 300, i.e. 270 = x − 150 and x = 420.
Hence the seven prizes are Rs. 420, Rs. 370, Rs. 320, Rs. 270, Rs. 220, Rs. 170 and Rs. 120.
items.concept: Formula for the sum
items.ocr: The printed stem reads "is to be used to given seven cash prizes"; kept as printed.

items.stem: A man repays a loan of Rs. 3250 by paying Rs. 20 in the first month and then increases the payment by Rs. 15 every month. How long will it take him to clear the loan?
items.answer:
The monthly payments form an AP with a = 20 and d = 15, and the total repaid is Sₙ = 3250.
Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] gives 3250 = n/2[40 + (n − 1)15], so 6500 = n[25 + 15n], i.e. 1300 = n[5 + 3n].
Hence 3n² + 5n − 1300 = 0, which factorises as (n − 20)(3n + 65) = 0, so n = 20 or n = −65/3.
A negative number of months is impossible, so n = 20. The man will clear the loan in 20 months.
items.concept: Formula for the sum
items.ocr: The printed working shows the middle step as "3n² + 65n − 60n − 1300 = 0" (a split of 5n) and then factorises to (n − 20)(3n + 65) = 0; the quadratic is 3n² + 5n − 1300 = 0, written that way here. Its root n = 20 is unchanged.

items.stem: A spiral is made up of successive semi-circles with centres alternately A and B starting with A, of radii 1 cm, 2 cm, 3 cm, …… as shown in the figure. What is the total length of spiral made up of eleven consecutive semi-circles? (Use π = 3.14)
items.answer:
Let l₁, l₂, …, l₁₁ be the lengths of the eleven semi-circles, whose radii are 1, 2, 3, …, 11 cm.
The length of a semi-circle of radius r is πr, so l₁ = π cm, l₂ = 2π cm, l₃ = 3π cm, …, l₁₁ = 11π cm.
Total length L = π + 2π + 3π + … + 11π = π(1 + 2 + 3 + … + 11) = π × (11 × 12)/2 = 66π.
With π = 3.14, L = 66 × 3.14 = 207.24 cm.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem: The ratio of the sums of first m and first n terms of an AP is m²:n². Show that the ratio of its mᵗʰ and nᵗʰ terms is (2m − 1):(2n − 1).
items.answer:
Let the first term be a and the common difference d.
Given Sₘ/Sₙ = m²/n², i.e. {m/2[2a + (m − 1)d]} ÷ {n/2[2a + (n − 1)d]} = m²/n².
Cancelling and cross-multiplying: [2a + (m − 1)d]/[2a + (n − 1)d] = (m²/n²) × (n/m) = m/n, so m[2a + (n − 1)d] = n[2a + (m − 1)d].
Expanding: 2am + mnd − md = 2an + mnd − nd, hence 2am − 2an = md − nd, i.e. 2a(m − n) = d(m − n), so d = 2a.
Now aₘ/aₙ = [a + (m − 1)d]/[a + (n − 1)d] = [a + (m − 1)2a]/[a + (n − 1)2a] = a(2m − 1)/a(2n − 1) = (2m − 1)/(2n − 1).
Hence aₘ : aₙ = (2m − 1) : (2n − 1), as required.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem: An AP consists of 37 terms. The sum of the three middle most terms is 225 and the sum of the past three terms is 429. Find the AP.
items.answer:
With 37 terms the middle term is the (37 + 1)/2 = 19ᵗʰ term. Let the three middle-most terms be (x − d), x and (x + d).
Their sum is (x − d) + x + (x + d) = 3x = 225, so x = 75, i.e. a₁₉ = 75.
Writing the AP about the middle term, the first term is x − 18d and the last three terms are (x + 16d), (x + 17d) and (x + 18d).
Their sum is 3x + 51d = 429, so 225 + 51d = 429, giving 51d = 204 and d = 4.
The first term is a₁ = x − 18d = 75 − 18 × 4 = 75 − 72 = 3, and a₂ = 3 + 4 = 7, while the last term is a₃₇ = 3 + 36 × 4 = 147.
Hence the AP is 3, 7, 11, …, 147.
items.concept: Formula for the nth term
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 SQP 2017

items.stem: The houses in a row are numbered consecutively from 1 to 49. Show that there exists a value of X such that sum of numbers of houses proceeding the house numbered X is equal to sum of the numbers of houses following X.
items.answer:
The house numbers are 1, 2, 3, …, x − 1, x, x + 1, …, 49.
The houses preceding X are 1, 2, …, (x − 1), whose sum is (x − 1)/2 × [1 + (x − 1)] = x(x − 1)/2.
The houses following X are (x + 1), …, 49, whose sum is (1 + 2 + … + 49) − (1 + 2 + … + x) = (49 × 50)/2 − x(x + 1)/2.
Setting the two equal: x(x − 1)/2 + x(x + 1)/2 = 49 × 25, so (x² − x + x² + x)/2 = 1225, i.e. 2x²/2 = 1225 and x² = 1225.
Since 1225 = 7 × 7 × 5 × 5, x = 7 × 5 = 35. Such a value exists, namely X = 35.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem:
Salary : In investigating different job opportunities, you find that firm A will start you at Rs 25,000 per year and guarantee you a raise of Rs 1,200 each year whereas firm B will start you at Rs 28,000 per year but will guarantee you a raise of only Rs 800 each year.
(i) Over a period of 15 years, how much would you receive from firm A?
(ii) Over a period of 15 years, how much would you receive from firm B?
(iii) What would be your annual salary at firm A for the tenth year?
(iv) What would be your annual salary at firm B for the tenth year?
items.answer:
With each firm the yearly salaries form an arithmetic sequence, so the money received over 15 years is S₁₅ = 15/2[2a₁ + 14d] = 15(a₁ + 7d).
(i) Firm A: a₁ = 25,000 and d = 1,200, so S₁₅ = 15(25,000 + 7 × 1,200) = 15 × 33,400 = Rs 501,000.
(ii) Firm B: a₁ = 28,000 and d = 800, so S₁₅ = 15(28,000 + 7 × 800) = 15 × 33,600 = Rs 504,000.
(iii) For the tenth year n = 10, so a₁₀ = a₁ + 9d. Firm A: a₁₀ = 25,000 + 9(1,200) = Rs 35,800.
(iv) Firm B: a₁₀ = 28,000 + 9(800) = Rs 35,200.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems
items.ocr: The printed answer list labels the fourth answer "(ii) Rs 35200"; it is the answer to part (iv) and is recorded as such. The photograph beside the question is decorative, so no figure is attached.

items.stem: Investment : Eleven years ago an investment earned Rs 7,000 for the year. Last year the investment earned Rs 14,000. If the earnings from the investment have increased the same amount each year, what is the yearly increase and how much income has accrued from the investment over the past 11 years?
items.answer:
The yearly earnings form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 7,000 and a₁₁ = 14,000.
aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d gives 14,000 = 7,000 + 10d, so 10d = 7,000 and d = Rs 700 per year.
The income accrued over the 11 years is S₁₁ = 11/2(a₁ + a₁₁) = 11/2(7,000 + 14,000) = 11/2 × 21,000 = Rs 115,500.
So the yearly increase is Rs 700 and the total income over the 11 years is Rs 115,500.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

items.stem:
Arc of a Baby Swing : When Mackenzie's baby swing is started, the first swing (one way) is a 30 inch arc. As the swing slows down, each successive arc is 1.5 inch less than the previous one.
(i) Find the length of the tenth swing.
(ii) How far Mackenzie has travelled during the 10 swings ?
items.answer:
The arcs form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 30 inch and d = −3/2 = −1.5 inch.
(i) a₁₀ = a₁ + 9d = 30 + 9(−3/2) = 30 − 27/2 = 30 − 13.5 = 16.5 inches.
(ii) S₁₀ = 10(a₁ + a₁₀)/2 = 10(30 + 16.5)/2 = 10(46.5)/2 = 232.5 inches.
So the tenth swing is 16.5 inches long and Mackenzie travels 232.5 inches during the 10 swings.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

items.stem:
Computer Animations : The animation on a new computer game initially allows the hero of the game to jump a (screen) distance of 10 inch over booby traps and obstacles. Each successive jump is limited to ¾ inch less than the previous one.
(i) Find the length of the seventh jump
(ii) Find the total distance covered after seven jumps.
items.answer:
The jumps form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 10 inch and d = −3/4 inch.
(i) a₇ = a₁ + 6d = 10 + 6(−3/4) = 10 − 9/2 = 5.5 inches.
(ii) S₇ = 7(a₁ + a₇)/2 = 7(10 + 5.5)/2 = 7(15.5)/2 = 54.25 inches.
So the seventh jump is 5.5 inches and the total distance covered after seven jumps is 54.25 inches.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

items.stem:
Seating Capacity : The Fox Theater creates a “theater in the round” when it shows any of Shakespeare's plays. The first row has 80 seats, the second row has 88, the third row has 96, and so on.
(i) How many seats are in the 10th row?
(ii) How many seats are in the 25th row?
(iii) If there is room for 25 rows, how many chairs will be needed to set up the theatre?
items.answer:
The seats per row form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 80 and d = 8.
(i) a₁₀ = 80 + (10 − 1)(8) = 80 + 72 = 152 seats.
(ii) a₂₅ = 80 + (25 − 1)(8) = 80 + 192 = 272 seats.
(iii) The chairs needed for 25 rows are S₂₅ = 25(a₁ + a₂₅)/2 = 25(80 + 272)/2 = 25(352)/2 = 4400 seats.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems
items.ocr: The book prints the third part with the label "(ii)" a second time; its own solution numbers it (iii), so it is written as (iii) here. The stem starts at the foot of one page and the third part and the photograph are on the next; the theatre photograph is decorative, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Sales Goals : At the time that I was newly hired, 100 sales per month was what I required. Each following month—the last plus 20 more, as I work for the goal of top sales award. When 2500 sales are thusly made, I get a holiday package.
(i) How many sales were made by this person in the seventh month?
(ii) What were the total sales after the 12th month?
(iii) Was the goal of 2500 total sales met after the 12th month?
items.answer:
The monthly sales form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 100 and d = 20.
(i) a₇ = 100 + (7 − 1)(20) = 100 + 120 = 220 sales in the seventh month.
(ii) a₁₂ = 100 + (12 − 1)(20) = 100 + 220 = 320, so S₁₂ = 12(a₁ + a₁₂)/2 = 12(100 + 320)/2 = 12(420)/2 = 2520 sales.
(iii) Since 2520 > 2500, yes — the goal of 2500 total sales was met after the 12th month.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems
items.ocr: The printed solution writes the seventh-month figure as "$220" (a stray dollar sign); it is 220 sales. The illustration beside the solution is decorative, so no figure is attached.

items.stem: Temperature Fluctuation: At 5 P.M. in Coldwater, the temperature was a chilly 36° F. If the temperature decreased by 3° F every half-hour for the next 7 hr, at what time did the temperature hit 0° F ?
items.answer:
The readings taken every half-hour form an arithmetic sequence 36°, 33°, 30°, 27°, ….
Counting from the first half-hourly drop, a₁ = 33, d = −3 and we need the term aₙ = 0.
aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d gives 0 = 33 + (n − 1)(−3) = 33 − 3n + 3 = 36 − 3n, so 3n = 36 and n = 12.
Twelve half-hours is 6 hours after 5 P.M., so the temperature hit 0° F at 11 P.M.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

items.stem:
Model Teachers' Earnings : According to the National Teachers Association, teachers in the India earned an average of Rs 30,532 in 2000. This amount has increased by approximately Rs 1472 per year.
(i) Write a formula for the nth term of the arithmetic sequence that models teachers' average earnings n years after 1999.
(ii) How much will India teachers earn, on average, by the year 2030?
items.answer:
The first term a₁ represents the earnings in 2000 (that is n = 1, one year after 1999), so a₁ = 30,532 and the yearly increase is d = 1,472.
(i) aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d = 30,532 + (n − 1)(1,472) = 30,532 + 1,472n − 1,472, so aₙ = 1472n + 29,060.
(ii) The year 2030 is 2030 − 1999 = 31 years after 1999, so n = 31 and a₃₁ = 1472 × 31 + 29,060 = 45,632 + 29,060 = 74,692.
Teachers are predicted to earn an average of Rs 74,692 by the year 2030.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems
items.ocr: The photograph beside the question is decorative, so no figure is attached. The second part of the solution finishes at the top of the next column.

items.stem:
Contest Prizes : A contest offers 15 prizes. The 1st prize is Rs 5000, and each successive prize is Rs 250 less than the preceding prize.
(i) What is the value of the 15th prize?
(ii) What is the total amount of money distributed in prizes?
items.answer:
The prizes form an arithmetic sequence Rs 5000, Rs 4750, Rs 4500, … with a₁ = 5000 and d = −250.
(i) a₁₅ = a₁ + (15 − 1)d = 5000 + 14(−250) = 5000 − 3500 = Rs 1500.
(ii) S₁₅ = 15/2(a₁ + a₁₅) = 15/2(5000 + 1500) = (15 × 6500)/2 = Rs 48,750.
So the 15th prize is Rs 1500 and Rs 48,750 is distributed in all.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem:
Bequests to Charity : At the time our mother left this Earth, she gave Rs 90000 to her children of birth. This we kept and each year added Rs 30000 more, as a lasting memorial from the children she bore. When Rs 4,20,000 is thusly attained, all goes to charity that her memory be maintained.
(i) What was the balance in the sixth year?
(ii) In what year was the goal of Rs 420,000 met?
items.answer:
The starting bequest is Rs 90,000 and Rs 30,000 is added each year, so the balance at the end of the first year is a₁ = 90,000 + 30,000 = Rs 1,20,000 and the yearly increase is d = 30,000.
(i) a₆ = a₁ + (6 − 1)d = 120,000 + 5(30,000) = 120,000 + 150,000 = Rs 270,000.
(ii) Putting aₙ = 420,000: 420,000 = 120,000 + (n − 1)(30,000), so (n − 1)(30,000) = 300,000 and n − 1 = 10, giving n = 11.
The balance in the sixth year was Rs 270,000 and the goal of Rs 420,000 was met in the 11th year.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

Its step "14 = 4 + n − 1" is also garbled; the arithmetic it carries out gives n = 11, the answer it prints. items.stem:
It takes 5 toothpicks to build the top trapezoid shown at below. You need 9 toothpicks to build 2 adjoined trapezoids and 13 toothpicks for 3 trapezoids.
(i) If 1000 toothpicks are available, how many trapezoids will be in the last complete row?
(ii) How many complete rows will there be?
(iii) How many toothpicks will you use to construct these rows?
(iv) Use the numbers in this problem to carefully describe the difference between a sequence and a series.
items.answer:
The toothpicks needed for successive rows are 5, 9, 13, …, an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 5 and d = 4.
(i) With Sₙ = 1000: 1000 = n/2[2 × 5 + (n − 1) × 4] = n[5 + 2(n − 1)] = 2n² + 3n, so 2n² + 3n − 1000 = 0.
n = [−3 ± √(3² − 4 × 2 × (−1000))]/(2 × 2) = (−3 ± √8009)/4 ≈ 21.62 or −23.12. Only a positive whole number makes sense, so n = 21 and the last complete row holds 21 trapezoids.
(ii) The number of trapezoids in a row equals the row number, so there are 21 complete rows.
(iii) S₂₁ = 21/2[2 × 5 + (21 − 1) × 4] = 21/2[10 + 80] = 21/2 × 90 = 945 toothpicks.
(iv) The numbers of toothpicks in each row, 5, 9, 13, …, form a sequence — a list of terms; the running totals of those numbers, 5, 14, 27, …, 945, form a series — the sum of the terms of that sequence.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem: Book Reading : On the first day of October an English teacher suggests to his students that they read five pages of a novel and every day thereafter increase their daily reading by two pages. If his students follow this suggestion, then how many pages will they read during October?
items.answer:
The pages read each day are 5, 7, 9, …, an arithmetic sequence with a = 5 and d = 2, and October has 31 days, so n = 31.
The pages read on the last day are a₃₁ = 5 + (31 − 1)(2) = 5 + 60 = 65.
The total for the month is S₃₁ = 31/2(a₁ + a₃₁) = 31/2(5 + 65) = 31/2 × 70 = 1085.
The students read 1085 pages during October.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem:
Increasing Salary : A lab technician has a salary of Rs 22,000 her first year and is due to get a Rs 500 raise each year,
(i) What will her salary be in her seventh year?
(ii) What is the total salary for 7 years of work for the lab technician ?
items.answer:
The yearly salaries form an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 22,000 and d = 500.
(i) a₇ = a₁ + (7 − 1)d = 22,000 + 6(500) = 22,000 + 3,000 = Rs 25,000.
(ii) S₇ = 7/2(a₁ + a₇) = 7/2(22,000 + 25,000) = 7/2 × 47,000 = Rs 164,500.
Her seventh-year salary is Rs 25,000 and the total for 7 years is Rs 164,500.

items.stem: Old Age Home : Your grandmother has assets of Rs 500,000. One option that she is considering involves an adult residential community for a six-year period beginning in 2020. The model aₙ = 1800n + 64130 describes yearly adult residential community costs n years after 2019. Does your grandmother have enough to pay for the facility?
items.answer:
The model describes costs n years after 2019, so n = 1 is the year 2020 and n = 6 is the year 2025 — the six years of the stay.
For 2020, a₁ = 1800 × 1 + 64,130 = Rs 65,930; for 2025, a₆ = 1800 × 6 + 64,130 = 10,800 + 64,130 = Rs 74,930.
The total cost of the six years is S₆ = 6/2(a₁ + a₆) = 3(65,930 + 74,930) = 3 × 140,860 = Rs 422,580.
Since Rs 422,580 is less than her assets of Rs 500,000, yes — she has enough to pay for the facility for the six-year period.
items.concept: Formula for the sum

items.stem:
TOWER OF PISA : To prove that objects of different weights fall at the same rate, Galileo dropped two objects with different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy. The objects hit the ground at the same time. When an object is dropped from a tall building, it falls about 16 feet in the first second, 48 feet in the second, and 80 feet in the third second, regardless of its weight.
(i) How many feet would an object fall in the sixth second?
(ii) How many feet would an object fall in the six second?
(iii) How many feet would an object fall in the eight second?
items.answer:
The distances fallen in successive seconds are 16, 48, 80, …, an arithmetic sequence with a₁ = 16 feet and d = 48 − 16 = 32 feet.
The distance fallen in the nᵗʰ second is aₙ = 16 + (n − 1)32 = 32n − 16 = 16(2n − 1).
(i) In the 6th second: a₆ = 16(2 × 6 − 1) = 16 × 11 = 176 feet.
(ii) The total fall in 6 seconds: S₆ = 6/2(a₁ + a₆) = 3(16 + 176) = 3 × 192 = 576 feet.
(iii) The total fall in 8 seconds: S₈ = 8/2[2 × 16 + (8 − 1) × 32] = 4[32 + 224] = 4 × 256 = 1024 feet.
items.concept: Using the formula in real problems

Its last two parts are both labelled "(ii)"; they answer (ii) and (iii). Parts (i) and (ii) of the stem read "sixth second" and "six second"; the solution reads them as the distance in the 6th second and the total over 6 seconds.
